meta_description: FinOps & Sustainable Computing from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Cost and carbon as engineering inputs: unit economics per workload with allocation coverage that reaches the invoice, rightsizing with teeth, zombie estates hunted on schedule — and sustainability reported from meters, not multipliers.
Nobody spends someone else's money carefully — allocate it first

Cloud cost fails as a monthly surprise. FinOps here is engineering: unit economics (cost per customer, per order, per model call) as first-class metrics, budgets wired into deployment paths, and rightsizing driven by measured utilization rather than quarterly panic.

Sustainability rides the same rails: carbon per unit of work, scheduling that follows clean-energy windows, and the waste ledger — idle GPUs, over-provisioned clusters, zombie environments — reported next to cost because they are the same problem.
Below: the failure modes that keep cloud bills foggy, the reference architecture of unit economics, and the console that trends cost and carbon together.
Four failure modes that keep cloud bills foggy
Every one of these hides real money in averages — the countermeasures allocate to the workload, trend the unit cost and hunt the zombies on a schedule.

widgets.title: Where the estate spend goes — split by controllable driver
widgets.note: Click segments to pin. Waste under 3% after the rightsizing pass — the segment to watch is AI inference, whose unit economics come from the GenAI platform's routing.

widgets.title: Unit cost by product line — the number teams move
widgets.note: Click to isolate. Unit costs are weekly numbers per team — the invoice is monthly and belongs to nobody; these belong to owners.

widgets.title: Commitment what-if — coverage, tier and demand variance
widgets.note: The savings curve flattens while strand risk rises — past ~75% coverage, each committed dollar buys less and risks more. High-variance demand should push coverage down, not up.

widgets.title: Deferrable-work scheduling — carbon intensity by hour × region
widgets.note: Hover cells to read regional carbon intensity by window. The 08–12 and 12–16 columns are the grid peak — deferrable jobs scheduled into 00–08 windows cut training footprint 30–40% at zero performance cost.

blocks.note: Reference program model: unit-cost and intensity bands from delivery benchmarks, not client data.
